correctness.rationale: For p=1 the kernel is a tensor product of exp(-a δ), whose exact Fourier coefficients a(1-(-1)^n e^{-aπ})/[π(a²+n²)] are strictly positive. For p>1 define F(t)=π^{-1}∫_0^π φ((t^p+s^p)^{1/p}) ds. The derivatives R_t(0,s)=0 and ∫R_tt≤1 justify F′(0)=0, F′ absolutely continuous and F′′∈L1; strict φ′<0 on antipodal radii gives F′(π)<0. Twice integrating by parts yields n² hat f(n,0)=((-1)^nF′(π)-F′(0))/π-o(1), negative for every sufficiently high even n. Compact-group Fourier positivity gives a finite-grid negative Gram witness. Independent quadrature checked exact p=1 product coefficients and negative modes for p=1.5,2,3,6. Near p↓1 numerical cutoffs are not exhaustive.
residual_risks: Numerical p=1.5 negativity requires much higher frequencies than p=2; bounded tests do not prove all fixed p>1.
No statement about p=infinity, nonproduct torus norms, or uniform finite-grid witness size.
